suppress.notes:
False positive: wrong artifact.
dependency-check matches org.eclipse.angus:angus-activation to the CPE cpe:2.3:a:eclipse:angus_mail, at LOW confidence. They are different libraries sharing a project name: angus-activation is the Jakarta Activation Framework (MIME type handling, DataHandler), whereas CVE-2025-7962 is SMTP header injection in Jakarta Mail / angus-mail via \r and \n in message content.
angus-mail is not on this classpath, and angus-activation has no SMTP code path to inject into. NVD's cited fix (2.0.4) does not exist either — the line ends at 2.0.3 (2.1.0-M1 unreleased) — so there is nothing to upgrade to.
Scoped to the angus-activation package at its exact version.

DOMPurify, bundled inside the swagger-ui webjar (swagger-ui 5.32.2, DOMPurify 3.3.2). XSS/mXSS CVEs in the sanitiser swagger-ui uses to render OpenAPI descriptions in the browser. NVD has not scored these; dependency-check treats unscored findings as failing at any threshold, which is what tripped the -Psecurity build after the CVSS >= 7 version fixes.
Suppressed rather than upgraded because it does not reach a user: - swagger-ui is disabled by default (springdoc.swagger-ui.enabled=false and api-docs.enabled=false in application.yml) and ENABLED ONLY in the dev profile; application-prod.yml sets both false explicitly. The UI is never served in production, so its bundled DOMPurify never executes there. - it is a dev authoring tool, not a student-facing surface. - springdoc 2.8.17 is already the latest on the Spring Boot 3.5 line; chasing a patched swagger-ui webjar for a prod-disabled component is disproportionate.
Scoped to DOMPurify 3.3.2: a swagger-ui upgrade changes this version and the match stops applying, forcing re-review. If swagger-ui is ever served in production, delete this and upgrade instead.
